_comment: Master content calendar. The Editor agent owns this file. Status flow: idea -> researched -> drafted -> in-review -> approved -> scheduled -> published. HUMAN GATE: a post may not move past 'in-review' to 'approved' without Will's explicit approval, and may not be 'scheduled'/'published' unless it is 'approved'. publishDate is the intended live date; the post stays draft:true until it is BOTH approved AND its publishDate has arrived (enforced by the weekly rebuild cron + a date check). Agents never set status to 'approved' or 'published' themselves.
leadTimeExperiment: May–Jun 2026 batch: 4 posts testing whether season-fit at publishDate+bookingLeadDays moves bookings. crabbers (strong-seasonal), tides-jellyfish (strong-seasonal forward ~60d), sauna (deliberate mismatch / control), recipes (evergreen baseline). Measure bookings 20–60d out via blog-metrics, then retest.
seasonTargeting: Readers booking today arrive ~bookingLeadDays later. The Editor targets the season the reader will EXPERIENCE (publishDate + bookingLeadDays), not the publish date. Seasonal/timely posts must land roughly 5-6 weeks before that lived season. bookingLeadDays is refreshed from content/metrics/airbnb-metrics.json (Gmail-derived). Conversion rate is intentionally NOT a blog KPI — it is Airbnb-listing-side. Track occupancy and booked-nights instead.

gate.rule: No transition into 'approved' or 'published' by any agent. Will approves in batches; each approved post auto-publishes on its publishDate via the weekly cron.

posts.note: CATEGORY CORRECTED: brief §6 places this post under Lifestyle (narrative/brand-building), not Travel. Calendar had it as Travel — brief wins. Flag for Will to confirm. | ANGLE: first-person narrative dawn scene — Will (or a guest) walks the dock before sunrise, pulls the crab pots the cottage provides, culls the catch, cooks it that morning. The how-to is embedded in the story, not a listicle. Warm, sensory, unhurried — it earns the Lifestyle label. | TARGET READER: prospective guests who are curious whether crabbing is genuinely accessible at the cottage, and travel/lifestyle readers searching 'crabbing Potomac River' or 'Virginia crabbing guide' who may not yet know the property exists. This is a soft-sell awareness post. | WHAT TO RESEARCH: (1) Blue crab season dates on the Potomac / Northumberland County — typical peak (late June–August), legal minimum size (5 inches point-to-point per VMRC), and the VMRC recreational license requirement for non-residents. (2) Practical how-to: baiting a crab pot with chicken necks vs. oily fish, how long to leave pots, how many the cottage provides, how to tell a male jimmy from a female sook. (3) Hull Creek-specific: brackish/mostly-fresh water note from brief §7 (shallow, good for kids); tide influence on crab pot placement. (4) Sensory/atmosphere details: pre-dawn dock sounds on Hull Creek, fog off the water, herons, smell of low tide — Will can supply firsthand, or researcher can note placeholders. (5) Cooking: steaming blues with Old Bay on the screened porch. One simple recipe beat (not the full recipes post — that is post #4). (6) Any local crabbing lore tied to the Northern Neck watermen culture (cross-reference with the later 'Oysters, Workboats, and Watermen' post to avoid duplication). | INTERNAL LINKS REQUIRED (≥2): (a) /activities/ — the activities hub page is live; link naturally when describing what the cottage makes possible. (b) /area/ — the Northern Neck overview page is live; link when contextualizing Hull Creek / Potomac geography. Optional third link: /journal/the-art-of-the-slow-weekend (already published) if the narrative calls for a 'slow morning' callback. | VOICE: Will's first-person or close third on a guest; editorial-coastal, not instructional. Warm but not cutesy. No shell emojis, no puns on 'crabby.' Drop cap on the opening paragraph per design system. | REVISION 2026-05-15: Rewritten per Will's voice-model feedback — cut from ~800 exhaustive words to ~620 focused words. Dropped: full culling how-to (jimmy/sook breakdown), bait section, detailed steaming instructions, regulations deep-dive, Lewis patent history block, tidal mechanics subsection. Kept: dawn sensory scene, dock/fog/osprey, one-sentence regulations pointer to mrc.virginia.gov, brief steaming beat, Maya quote, both internal links, one CTA.
